placements.why: This envelope introduces the first organizational-strategy category this repo needs: a place for decisions about deployment/release infrastructure controls (the signed-manifest gate, its scope). Nothing in the supplied strata (which is empty) covers this, and the content is squarely about technical release architecture rather than opportunity, strategy, product, org-process, proof, templates, or calibration. Minting standalone with no parent, per the rule that a strata mint usually needs none.
placements.title: Release infrastructure becomes a governed gate, not an open pipe
placements.theme: Technical deployment infrastructure for Meridian is organized around enforced verification checkpoints rather than unrestricted flow.

placements.title: Deployment shifts from ad-hoc trust to enforced signed verification
placements.theme: Meridian deployments must clear a signed release-manifest gate, owned and scoped explicitly, because unsigned artifacts have already reached staging and cannot be allowed to again.
placements.why: src-1 and src-3 state the same directional requirement (signed manifest before shipping) in prose and structured form; src-4 fixes where that requirement binds; src-5 fixes who holds it; src-2 is the fact/incident (two unsigned artifacts reaching staging) that motivates and evidences the same governance shift rather than standing as its own theme. Together these are facets of one durable subject — how Meridian deployments are gated and by whom — that future envelopes about this gate's evolution, exceptions, or incidents will keep feeding, satisfying the narrative grain test. No existing leaf was available to reuse since the supplied graph structure is empty.
